intended_object: The algebra map f : A → C viewed as a morphism of algebras over the invariant ring E = {a ∈ A | f a = g a} (the equalizer subalgebra). Here A is an E-algebra through the inclusion and C is an E-algebra through f. Inferred from the docstring and from its use as one leg of `kernelPairComparison`, the map A ⊗_E A → C.
explanation: The body just takes the ring map of f and checks that it is compatible with the E-algebra structures: f(b·x) = f(b)·f(x) for b in E. That is the right check for the local instance making C an E-algebra via f. So the definition is correct, but it only re-bundles f with a different base ring. Its job is to supply the left leg to `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` when building `kernelPairComparison`. Mathematically this is the same map f, not a new object, so it is a technical bundling device. If it were judged as a mathematical object it would be faithful: it works for arbitrary commutative rings S, A, C and needs no extra hypotheses.
